title: Phase 1 acceptance coverage
text: Phase 1 acceptance coverage The automated tests execute the installed Qiskit/Aer engine, FastAPI application, and a temporary SQLite database. Compiler, simulation, and persistence results are not mocked. This document is a coverage guide; the final engineering report records the commands and outcomes that were actually executed. | Requirement | Automated evidence | | --- | --- | | QORE-IR version, gate order, control/target and classical mapping | backend/tests/test_quantum.py | | Metric definitions, counts and actual compiler differences | backend/tests/test_quantum.py | | Bell-state samples, seeded repeatability, exact shot totals, theoretical probabilities and calculated TVD | backend/tests/test_quantum.py | | Little-endian output labels and swapped classical mapping | backend/tests/test_quantum.py | | Original circuit preserved; real simplification; honest zero improvement | backend/tests/test_quantum.py | | Full-operator comparison, global phase, incorrect transformation, mapping mismatch and size limit | backend/tests/test_quantum.py | | Arbitrary imports/calls, attribute traversal, file access, comprehensions, unsupported constructs and malformed source rejected | backend/tests/test_security.py | | Source, register, instruction and shot caps | backend/tests/test_security.py and backend/tests/test_api.py | | Project create, rename, save, open and list | backend/tests/test_api.py | | Bell parse → simulate → optimize → validate → save → reopen | backend/tests/test_api.py | | Immutable historical snapshots after project edits and application restart | backend/tests/test_api.py | | Source hash mismatch, unknown references and incorrect run kinds rejected | backend/tests/test_api.py | | Structured HTTP errors, recovery after a failed run and optional AI unavailable | backend/tests/test_api.py | Browser acceptance procedure Run the backend and frontend using the repository setup instructions. In the running application: 1. Open the Bell-state example and inspect editable, highlighted source. 2. Parse and verify that the SVG shows H on q0, CX from q0 to q1, and the measurement/classical connections from the returned IR. 3. Run the simulator with 1,024 shots and seed 42. Confirm counts total 1,024, only 00/11 occur, and theoretical values are visibly distinguished from sampled probabilities. 4. Optimize and inspect separate original/candidate diagrams, actual metrics, settings and validation evidence. Confirm that the editor still contains the original source. 5. Save an experiment, edit the source, and reopen the saved experiment. Confirm the historical label, original source, run configuration, counts and compiler evidence are restored. 6. Edit the source again and confirm live results are cleared. Run again and confirm new execution replaces the historical context. 7. Make an unsaved edit and switch projects. Confirm the discard decision is explicit. 8. Use the redundant-gates example to verify an actual simplification. Approve the candidate explicitly and confirm that the optimization snapshot retains the original. 9. Trigger invalid syntax and confirm the error is visible, then correct it and run successfully. 10. Open Intelligence without configured credentials and confirm the unavailable state leaves the core workflow usable. 11. Check a narrow viewport and keyboard navigation. Record screenshots of the working application. Passing API tests alone does not establish that these browser steps have passed. Browser outcomes and any unverified steps must be reported separately.

title: Automated quality reviews
text: Automated quality reviews QORE has an active Codex daily review coordinator scheduled for 09:00 in Asia/Kolkata. Scheduling is managed by the Codex heartbeat attached to the project conversation; this repository does not install an operating-system task or a server cron job. | Dedicated review agent | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | Studio and Explorer | Editing, database autosave, refresh/offline recovery, folder operations, 48-hour Trash and Undo, layout and accessibility | | Quantum Lab and Qiskit | Analytic reference circuits, probabilities, noise, Bloch purity, matrices, supported syntax and bounds | | Forge | Compiler candidates, operator equivalence, source hashes, measurement mapping and approval | | Identity and Ledger | Email confirmation and availability, verified sessions, account separation, RLS and immutable restoration | | AI Assistant | Secondary sidebar, grounded circuit/results context, stale-response prevention and safe failures | | Security and Secrets | Source/configuration scanning, credentials, Docker boundaries, dependency advisories and IDE safety | | Organization and Scalability | Module boundaries, types, containers, persistence, worker budgets, concurrency and performance | | SEO and Google Discoverability | Public metadata, crawlability, sitemap, canonical URLs, accessibility and indexing boundaries | The coordinator dispatches these scopes in batches within the available agent limit, then consolidates actionable findings into a daily report. If delegation is unavailable, it completes the scopes sequentially. It prepares safe fixes in an isolated branch/worktree and does not automatically push, merge, deploy, rotate credentials, or modify live user data. The coordinator uses the repeatable local baseline below, reviews its evidence, and directs focused investigation where a check fails or a meaningful improvement is identified. The specialist review complements the executable checks; a successful build alone does not establish security, accessibility, scalability, or quantum correctness. Run the same baseline manually From the repository root, with project dependencies installed: powershell & ".\.venv\Scripts\python.exe" scripts/daily_quality_report.py The script performs four sequential stages: | Stage | Checks | Timeout | | --- | --- | ---: | | Security and secret exposure | Source/configuration credentials, Dockerfiles, environment variants, Git exposure, ignore rules, IDE settings, configuration heuristics | 120 seconds | | Frontend health | TypeScript, production build, frontend secret isolation, structural checks and API contract heuristics | 180 seconds | | Backend regression suite | All tests in backend/tests, including anonymous browser isolation and workspace boundaries | 600 seconds | | Quantum and ledger acceptance | Real API/worker/Aer execution, reference comparisons, noise, matrices, Forge equivalence and immutable evidence restoration | 180 seconds | Every stage runs even if an earlier stage fails, so the resulting report identifies independent problems. The script exits with a nonzero status if a stage fails, times out, or does not produce a fresh valid report. Timed-out process trees are terminated. Evidence Reports are written to the ignored local evidence/ directory: - daily_quality_report.json and .md: stage outcomes, timings, numeric summaries and individual report locations. - security_report.json and .md: findings with fully masked credentials. - frontend_health_report.json and .md: frontend checks and diagnostics. - production_acceptance.json and .md: quantitative quantum and ledger results. The daily aggregator captures child output in memory and retains only numeric summaries. It does not copy arbitrary compiler, provider, or test output into its logs. Provider credential variables are removed from child environments. Acceptance uses temporary SQLite storage and explicitly prevents loading the user's .env; it never operates on live user projects or accounts. The baseline does not push commits, deploy releases, install dependencies, or change external services. The schedule and specialist responsibilities can be updated through the project conversation. Repository quality gate .github/workflows/quality.yml runs the same baseline on pushes to editing, main, and production, and on pull requests targeting release branches. It also has a daily 09:00 India schedule and a manual trigger. The daily GitHub schedule becomes active when the workflow is present on the repository's default branch. This complements the Codex specialist review and can run without the desktop app being open. The workflow has read-only repository permissions, pinned action revisions, a frontend lockfile, an isolated Python environment, bounded execution, and a numeric job summary. It receives no provider credentials and does not deploy, merge, or publish user data. Use its checks when reviewing the editing branch before release promotion. Secret-scanning boundaries The scanner checks source files, extensionless Dockerfiles/Containerfiles, .env.example, and .env. variants. It recognizes modern secret key formats and legacy JWTs whose decoded payload explicitly grants the service_role role. Tokens are never printed, including partial prefixes or suffixes. A public anon JWT is not treated as a privileged credential merely because it is a JWT. An ignored server .env is left unread. Frontend environment files remain in scope, and Git's index is checked by filename to identify tracked sensitive paths even when ignore rules exist. Generated dependency, build, browser-profile, capture, and media directories are pruned. An unreadable source/configuration file produces a finding rather than a successful secret-scan result. These are detection heuristics, not a guarantee that every possible credential format or vulnerability will be found. Windows file ACLs require a separate host permission inspection; the scanner does not claim to verify them. Quantum verification scope Acceptance covers three-qubit GHZ preparation, a two-qubit marked-state Grover example, coherent deferred-measurement teleportation, the original four-qubit openqasm/qaoa_cut.qasm regression sequence, noisy outcomes versus an ideal reference, displayed unitary orthonormality, Forge operator equivalence, invalid input rejection, and immutable ledger restoration after restart. All quantum execution is local simulation. The configured source, qubit, operation, shot, timeout, and operator-validation limits apply. These checks do not assert support for arbitrary Python, every Qiskit API, hardware execution, or a proven optimization advantage. The historical QAOA sequence is a test fixture, not an automatically created user file.

title: QI Assistant: quantum intelligence across QORE
text: QI Assistant: quantum intelligence across QORE QI Assistant provides explanations and controlled workspace actions beside every QORE view. Its dedicated, VS Code-style secondary sidebar stays available in Studio, Lab, Forge, and Ledger. It receives only bounded context assembled by the application and can invoke explicit local actions such as opening a view, showing the terminal, creating a blank file, simulating, or optimizing. Generated text cannot silently edit source, certify evidence, or access the provider key. !Assistant concept(../assets/animations/assistant.gif) What context it receives The request includes the active view, file name, workspace summary, sanitized diagnostics, optional circuit source, and the question. It can reference a simulation ID and optimization ID. The backend checks those IDs against the opaque browser workspace, expected kind, successful execution, and submitted source hash before assembling provider context. This means a result cannot be attached merely because its ID is known. A result from an older source version is rejected as a mismatch. The frontend clears stale answers when the view, file, or attached run changes. Both client and server rules are important: a stale screen is confusing, and an unchecked backend reference would be a data-integrity problem. When results are absent, an answer should say that it is reasoning from source or theory. It must not invent shot counts, hardware jobs, or validation evidence. The instruction distinguishes theoretical probabilities, finite-shot simulator output, and hardware data; QORE supplies no hardware runs through this interface. Ask a useful question Good questions specify the object and evidence you want explained. For example: why does the ideal GHZ distribution have only two outcomes; why is each local Bloch sphere centered; what does a mapping q0 - c1 mean; which reported metric changed after compilation; or why is Forge validation unavailable for this circuit size? If you ask for an improvement, request a small proposal with an expected effect and a way to test it. Read the proposed source yourself. Apply changes through the editor and rerun the circuit. An explanation of equivalence is not the same as the recorded full-operator check. Avoid asking the model to infer hidden implementation details from a chart alone. Give the relevant source and actual result context. For a comparison, specify whether shots, seed, method, and noise are fixed. Otherwise an answer can confuse a sampling change with an algorithm change. Authority boundaries The model cannot edit your buffer, submit a hardware job, or approve a compiler candidate. QI's local command layer may call already-visible QORE actions such as Run Simulation or Optimize Circuit only after the user explicitly types or clicks that action. Numerical checks remain in the quantum engine, and applying source changes remains an explicit user action. Circuit source and questions are untrusted input. Text inside them does not become a system instruction that can grant the assistant more authority. A malicious comment saying to reveal credentials or ignore evidence does not change the backend's provider-key isolation or source-matching checks. The model can still make reasoning mistakes. Verify a mathematical claim against the result data and a small independent calculation. For example, a centered local Bloch vector in an entangled pure register is expected; an answer calling that a failed state preparation should be corrected using the reduced-density-matrix interpretation. Provider configuration and availability The optional provider key and model configuration live on the server. The frontend never accepts a model-provider credential in request JSON and never bundles one in a VITE_ variable. If the provider is not configured, QORE returns a clear unavailable answer and the core quantum workflow continues. Provider network failures, an empty response, or an invalid configured model produce bounded failure behavior. The application should not replace an actual numerical result with a generated fallback. Retry only after reading the availability message and preserving your current work. The server currently limits assistant traffic to ten requests per browser workspace per minute and two concurrent provider calls per process. Admission waiting is bounded to two seconds, and provider requests have a timeout. These are application budgets, not a complete provider billing policy. Operators should configure provider-side spending and retention controls separately. Privacy and data handling Invoking the assistant sends the assembled question and context to the configured Gemini service. Browser-local storage does not imply that an optional provider request stays on the device. Do not include secrets, personal data, or confidential research unless the provider policy and your authorization permit that use. The assistant does not need passwords, access tokens, database credentials, or environment files. Keep those out of source comments and questions. Redaction in error displays is useful but is not a reason to submit sensitive material in the first place. On a shared computer, use separate browser profiles and clear QORE site data only after exporting important work. Browser storage is not an encrypted vault. If a support report includes an assistant issue, use a minimal nonprivate circuit and sanitized availability/error information. Troubleshooting If an answer refers to old source, confirm the active buffer and attached run IDs; stale responses should clear on context change. If a request returns mismatch, rerun the current source rather than forcing an old run ID. If the sidebar is crowded on a laptop, close Explorer or the assistant while inspecting a matrix. If the service is busy, wait before retrying rather than opening parallel requests. Use the Lab manual(quantum-lab.md) for numerical semantics, Forge(forge.md) for verification, and security(../operations/security.md) for server/provider boundaries. The assistant is most useful when it helps you inspect those primary sources of evidence more effectively.

title: Forge: compiler candidates and verification
text: Forge: compiler candidates and verification Forge is QORE's compiler review surface. It generates a candidate circuit, compares resource metrics, and records a numerical equivalence assessment. The user decides whether to apply the candidate. Keeping generation, verification, and approval separate makes the transformation inspectable instead of treating a successful compiler response as proof of correctness. !Forge concept(../assets/animations/forge.gif) Prepare a meaningful comparison Open a supported circuit and make sure the source is saved or otherwise preserved. Record the question you are asking: remove redundant gates, compare optimization levels, or inspect a normalized basis. A short circuit with deliberate redundancy is a good first test because the expected behavior can be checked independently. python from qiskit import QuantumCircuit qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 2) qc.h(0) qc.h(0) qc.x(1) qc.x(1) qc.cx(0, 1) qc.cx(0, 1) qc.measure(0, 0) qc.measure(1, 1) The pairs in the unitary prefix cancel, so its net action is identity. Forge can expose how a compiler represents that fact. Do not assume that every realistic circuit has the same amount of removable redundancy. Candidate generation Choose optimization level 0, 1, 2, or 3 and a seed. The backend parses the source, separates the unitary prefix from terminal measurements, and transpiles the prefix into the supported u and cx basis. It then reattaches the measurement suffix with the original destinations. Optimizing only the prefix matters. A measurement-aware pass may remove a final phase operation without changing computational-basis counts, but that can alter the stronger full-operator property that QORE checks. Preserving the prefix's action makes the verification claim clearer. The current Forge does not configure a physical coupling map, device calibration, or hardware execution target. It is a basis and optimization experiment. A higher level can cost more compilation time and does not guarantee fewer gates, lower depth, or a better result under every metric. Read metrics using one convention Gate count counts unitary instructions and excludes measurement and barrier. Two-qubit count includes exactly two-qubit unitary instructions. A CCX is one three-qubit instruction before decomposition, so converting it into a one-/two-qubit basis can increase the apparent gate count while preserving semantics. Depth follows the recorded circuit-depth convention, including measurements and excluding barriers. Compare the original and candidate under the same convention. An absolute or relative resource difference is not a prediction of wall-clock speed on an unconfigured quantum device. If an original metric is zero, a relative percentage may be undefined rather than infinite. Read the numerical before and after values. A candidate should be judged according to the intended objective, not just a green reduction badge. Operator comparison For circuits of up to six qubits, QORE constructs both full unitary operators. It aligns one global phase using their overlap and computes the maximum absolute elementwise residual. Validation succeeds when that residual is at most 1e-9 and register sizes and terminal measurement mappings match. This compares every basis input rather than only the default all-zero state. Two different circuits can produce the same output for one input and still fail full-operator comparison. A histogram match at finite shots is a weaker and statistically different observation. The response records method, qubit count, operator dimension, maximum error, tolerance, process fidelity, global-phase difference, and mapping evidence where available. Process fidelity is supporting numerical evidence; the actual acceptance check is the maximum residual after phase alignment. Understand every status | Status | Meaning | | --- | --- | | validated | Recorded operator and mapping checks passed within scope | | failed | A checked structural or numerical property differed | | unavailable | The check was outside the supported scope, including more than six qubits | | inconclusive | The numerical comparison could not complete | Unavailable and inconclusive are not passes. A ten-qubit simulation may be supported while its full-operator verification is unavailable. Keep these different caps visible when reporting an experiment. Review and apply Inspect candidate source and the circuit representation. Read warnings and validation, then compare the terminal mapping. Applying the candidate is explicit. The assistant cannot approve it, and a generated explanation does not replace the recorded numerical check. Applying changes the workspace source and invalidates live results attached to the old text. Run the new circuit to obtain fresh sampled evidence. The original immutable run remains in the Ledger, so a rejected or abandoned proposal does not erase its provenance. If you want a before/after study, save distinct experiments with the same simulation settings. Their source hashes may differ even when unitary behavior is equivalent, because hashes identify text rather than mathematics. Include optimization level and seed in the comparison record. Common misunderstandings A smaller circuit is not automatically faster on an unspecified device. Equal counts do not prove equal operators. A validated ideal transformation does not prove that two physical implementations have identical noise. A global phase is ignored because it does not affect the isolated circuit's observable behavior, but arbitrary relative phases are not ignored. If verification fails, retain the original source and inspect register sizes, mapping, and numerical residual. If compilation fails, reduce the program to supported operations and check the resource limit. If validation is unavailable, report that limitation rather than describing the candidate as proven. The equivalence lesson(../quantum/equivalence.md) develops these distinctions with examples.

title: Quantum Lab: simulation and evidence
text: Quantum Lab: simulation and evidence Quantum Lab turns a supported circuit into inspectable numerical evidence. It connects the source and settings to Qiskit Aer, then presents measured counts, empirical probabilities, an ideal reference, state views, metrics, and execution metadata. Each view answers a different question; the Lab keeps their provenance attached rather than treating every visual as a hardware measurement. !Quantum Lab concept(../assets/animations/lab.gif) From source to execution The active source is parsed into QORE-IR and checked against the circuit allowlist and resource bounds. Shot-based simulation requires at least one explicit terminal measurement. No unitary operation may follow the measurement suffix. Dynamic measurement-controlled programs are outside this runtime. The API admits a bounded number of jobs, runs the worker, and records the result as a historical run. A source hash identifies the exact submitted text. Editing source clears live results while the prior run remains available through the Ledger. The console and output panel refer to attached results, not an invented running shell session. Choose settings with purpose Shots determine the number of sampled measurements. Use enough shots to make the expected effect visible, but do not assume that more shots compensate for a wrong circuit or incorrect bit mapping. The supported range is 1–100,000. Seed controls simulator and compilation randomness under the same compatible implementation; it is not a guarantee of identical output after every software update. The API accepts statevector, matrix_product_state, or stabilizer. These methods have different compatibility and performance characteristics. Stabilizer simulation is appropriate for compatible Clifford circuits and can reject gates outside that family. Statevector is a straightforward starting point for the small circuits supported by QORE. Matrix product state performance depends on circuit structure, not just qubit count. Noise and readout-error settings configure simulator models. They do not import a real device's current calibration. Inspect the returned backend label, method, and noise flags to see what was used. A model setting is part of the experiment and belongs in any comparison you preserve. Counts and probabilities counts is a map from displayed classical bitstrings to nonnegative shot counts. Their sum must equal the requested shots. probabilities divides each count by shots and includes zero-probability outcomes in the returned empirical distribution. An absent observed key does not establish that an event is mathematically impossible. theoretical_probabilities is calculated from the ideal noiseless premeasurement state using the same qubit-to-classical mapping. This reference remains ideal even when sampled output uses noise. Keep the reference and sample distinct when explaining a divergence. For a GHZ circuit, the ideal distribution is one half on 000 and 111. Finite counts will fluctuate. With readout error, other strings can occur. Neither effect means the bitstring convention changed. Read measurement(../quantum/measurement.md) before interpreting a nontrivial mapping. Total variation distance The Lab reports TVD = 0.5 sum(abs(p_sample(s) - p_ideal(s))). Zero means the two distributions in that comparison match exactly. Values approach one as their probability mass separates. TVD here combines finite sampling fluctuation with any modeled-noise difference; it is not a direct measure of quantum-state fidelity. At low shots, a moderate TVD can arise from sampling alone. Compare repeated seeds or increase shots before attributing every difference to a circuit bug. At high shots, a persistently different distribution may indicate noise, source, mapping, or implementation differences. Read the surrounding metadata before drawing a conclusion. State views and their limits Statevector amplitudes describe ideal coherent evolution from the initial all-zero register. Their squared magnitudes determine ideal basis probabilities. Relative phase can matter for later interference even when it does not change the current basis histogram. Display values are rounded for reading. Bloch vectors are calculated from each qubit's reduced density matrix. Entanglement can make a local state mixed, with a vector inside the sphere. The global register can remain pure. These ideal local-state and amplitude displays are limited to six qubits; larger supported runs can still provide sampled output. The unitary matrix is available up to four qubits. It describes the unitary prefix on every computational-basis input and excludes measurement. A four-qubit circuit has a 16-by-16 operator, so the matrix view needs space and scrolling. The display cap is lower than the six-qubit verification cap because human-readable rendering and numerical validation are different operations. Metadata and bit ordering Execution metadata belongs below the primary output so you can inspect the scientific result at full width. It records backend, shots, seed, noise configuration, duration, timestamps, and versions. Duration is an observed execution measurement, not a service-level promise. Displayed bitstrings read the highest classical index on the left and c0 on the right. The mapping can differ from qubit index order. Unmeasured classical bits are zero. For q0 - c1 and q1 - c0, the left character describes qubit zero's measured destination. Always use the recorded mapping rather than guessing from circuit-wire positions. Metrics and circuit inspection Gate count excludes measurements and barriers. Two-qubit gate count counts instructions acting on exactly two qubits. A three-qubit gate counts as one unitary instruction before decomposition. Depth follows the circuit-depth convention with measurements included and barriers excluded. A change in basis can alter gate count without implying a proportional speedup on hardware. The circuit diagram and generated QASM provide additional ways to inspect what was compiled. QORE-IR is the shared semantic representation used by these views. Compare that representation and the source hash when diagnosing an unexpected result. A reliable experiment loop Predict a small circuit analytically. Fix the source, shots, seed, method, and noise settings. Run and check totals. Compare ideal reference, sampled counts, local state, and mapping. Save the evidence before varying one parameter. This approach makes a chart explainable and a discrepancy diagnosable. If a job is busy, retry after the active jobs finish. If it times out, reduce complexity and review host resources. If a state view is absent, check its display limit. If the output differs from expectation, first inspect source identity and mapping, then noise and method. See noise and sampling(../quantum/noise-sampling.md) for a deeper statistical treatment.

title: Research Ledger: immutable experiment evidence
text: Research Ledger: immutable experiment evidence Research Ledger preserves the context behind a result. Editable workspace files answer what you are working on now. A historical run answers what was submitted and what happened. An experiment groups source, parsed representation, configuration, versions, and referenced execution evidence into an immutable snapshot. Keeping these objects separate prevents routine editing from silently changing the record of an earlier experiment. !Research evidence concept(../assets/animations/ledger.gif) Files, projects, runs, and experiments An Explorer entry is editable source stored under an account path. Legacy named projects are separately stored source records that can be associated with runs. A simulation or optimization request produces a run record with a kind, original source, source hash, configuration, and result or recorded error. An experiment is a named snapshot that can include source-matched simulation and optimization evidence. These distinctions matter for deletion and recovery. Workspace Trash covers editable file/folder entries. Deleting a file does not mutate a historical run or rewrite an experiment's embedded source. A service-level backup policy may cover several tables, but the two-day file Trash mechanism is not a general undo system for every data object. What a snapshot retains The server parses source when creating an experiment. It stores QORE-IR version, canonical operations, metrics, warnings, source and source hash, and dependency versions. Referenced successful runs can attach the simulation and optimization results that belong to that same text. Simulation evidence includes settings such as shots, seed, method, modeled noise, backend, counts, ideal probabilities, and execution duration. Optimization evidence includes original/candidate representations, resource differences, compiler settings, and numerical validation. A future reader should be able to distinguish a predicted distribution, a sampled result, and a compiler claim. The hash is a content identifier, not a signature of execution correctness. Two circuits with different formatting can have different source hashes and the same semantics. A malicious or broken system could hash incorrect data consistently. Reproducibility therefore requires recorded methods, tests, access controls, and independent interpretation in addition to hashes. Source-matched attachments Before attaching a run, the API checks ownership, kind, successful completion, and source hash. A simulation ID cannot stand in for an optimization ID. A result from a different source version produces a conflict rather than being quietly attached to the current code. This prevents a common experiment error: editing the circuit and saving an old attractive chart as if it belonged to the new version. The frontend also clears live results on source changes. The server check remains necessary because a client display rule alone cannot enforce data integrity. Create a useful experiment Start with a specific question, such as whether one QAOA angle improves expected cut value under fixed sampling settings. Save the working source. Run it, inspect the backend and mapping, and verify that the output is consistent with the question. Add a compiler result only if that comparison is part of the experiment. Choose a name that identifies intent. GHZ readout-error comparison is more useful than test2. Keep a narrative note in your workspace or external research record describing expected behavior, variable changes, and interpretation. The preserved numerical evidence is most useful when the hypothesis is also clear. Do not attach a failed or stale result simply to fill every field. An experiment with parsed source and a clearly described limited scope is better than one that suggests it contains a successful run when it does not. Reopen and extend history Open an experiment to inspect its preserved source and evidence. Historical source is treated as historical context rather than a writable copy of the stored snapshot. Clone or explicitly begin editing to create a new working version. This makes the transition from observation to new experiment deliberate. The old snapshot stays unchanged. Applying a Forge candidate or editing a workspace file does not rewrite it. To compare a new result, create another named experiment. Keep the same settings when isolating a source change, and keep the same source when isolating a noise or sampling change. Read errors as evidence Run recording also preserves expected execution failures with configuration and an error envelope. A failed run is not a successful numerical output. It can still help explain why a later experiment changed source or settings. Use the status and error code instead of treating an empty chart as a zero-probability result. Recorded errors are sanitized. Raw provider responses, environment variables, or credentials do not belong in a historical snapshot. A support report should refer to a sanitized error and minimal nonprivate source rather than exporting another person's complete record. Reproducibility and its limits Source, seed, configuration, and package versions make rerunning a study much more precise. They do not guarantee identical floating-point values or sampled counts across framework versions, CPU platforms, or implementation changes. Numerical algorithms and random-number behavior can change. Report comparison tolerances and statistical uncertainty rather than promising bit-for-bit reproducibility everywhere. An immutable record is also not an automatic backup. Operators must maintain database backup, retention, restore testing, and incident response. Users should export important research according to the available workflow and keep independent copies when the work matters beyond one hosted instance. Privacy and access Hosted Ledger records are owner-scoped. The backend verifies session identity, then uses the user's access boundary for database requests. Composite relationships prevent linking another account's project or run. Run and experiment storage is append-oriented rather than offering arbitrary in-place history rewriting. Signing out clears visible private evidence. Optional assistant requests can transmit the active circuit and attached results to the configured model provider, so decide whether that provider is appropriate for your data before invoking it. Read assistant privacy(assistant.md) and backup operations(../operations/backup-recovery.md) before adopting QORE for sensitive research.

title: State World and visual state inspection
text: State World and visual state inspection State World is QORE's spatial view of simulation evidence. It complements distributions, amplitudes, Bloch vectors, and matrices with interactive 3D inspection. The shared graphite gradient and glass controls keep it part of the same workbench. Motion helps navigation and emphasis; the numerical readout remains the authority for probability, phase, and state identity. Different visualizations, different objects A quantum register state, a one-qubit reduced state, a unitary transformation, and a histogram are not interchangeable. State World presents basis-state information. A Bloch sphere presents one qubit's reduced state. An amplitude table exposes complex coefficients. A unitary matrix describes a transformation on every possible input. A histogram shows sampled classical outcomes. These views can agree with one another without looking similar. An entangled GHZ state has two nonzero basis probabilities, yet every local Bloch vector is at the sphere center. A phase change can leave a histogram unchanged and still alter interference later. Understanding the object behind each view avoids reading decorative movement as an additional measurement. Basis states in State World Basis labels identify bitstrings under the view's stated convention. Interactive selection lets you inspect a state without relying on the size or glow of a moving element. Read the associated probability and sampled count where available. A missing sampled count does not imply an exactly zero ideal probability at finite shots. Use the backend result as the reference when comparing visual emphasis. The visual scene may compress dynamic ranges for legibility. Camera angle, orbit, glow, or a selected-node highlight does not create a new physical observable. Any conclusion about distribution quality belongs to the returned probabilities, counts, and TVD. The Lab's metadata remains attached below the primary result. Check source hash and configuration before comparing two scenes. Source edits clear stale live results; immutable historical runs can still be reopened through the Ledger. Focused Bloch mode Focused mode enlarges the selected qubit inside the shared gradient surface. Drag to inspect its 3D geometry and axes, then read numerical information below the sphere. The vector coordinates are expectation values of the Pauli X, Y, and Z operators for that qubit's reduced density matrix. The vector radius is sqrt(xx + yy + zz). A pure one-qubit state lies on the sphere surface. A mixed state lies inside it. The maximally mixed state is at the center. The readout's purity is Tr(rhorho), equal to (1 + rr)/2; radius itself is not purity. For an unentangled |0 qubit, expect z approximately one. H maps it to the positive x direction. A Y-axis rotation changes x and z according to the angle. In a Bell or GHZ state, the local vector can vanish. These are ideal model states computed before measurement, not reconstructed device tomography. All-qubit mode All-qubit mode displays several spheres on one shared background instead of enclosing each in a separate card. Sphere sizes adapt to the selected qubit count and available width. Axes and interaction remain consistent with focused mode. A laptop viewport may require a smaller arrangement or scrolling when labels and readouts need space. Use the common numerical convention when comparing qubits. The spheres describe separate reduced states, so they do not directly draw the full entanglement structure between them. Equal local vectors do not mean the full register states are equal. A set of local marginals cannot generally reconstruct all multi-qubit correlations. Amplitudes and phase An amplitude is a complex number a + ib. Its probability is aa + bb; its phase is the complex argument. QORE displays real and imaginary parts, magnitude, phase, and probability within the supported size. Values are rounded to make tables readable, and tiny components can be omitted under the documented display threshold. Two states can have identical basis probabilities with different relative phases. Prepare H, apply Z, then apply H again to see phase become a different output probability. A single amplitude table row does not carry the normalization or relative-phase context of the whole state, so inspect the complete relevant state before making an inference. Matrix inspection Unitary display is available for up to four qubits. A two-qubit operator is four by four, a three-qubit operator eight by eight, and a four-qubit operator sixteen by sixteen. Each column is the output amplitude vector for one basis input. Rows identify output basis states. A cell's magnitude is not a shot frequency. It describes an amplitude of the transformation. Squaring magnitudes gives basis transition probabilities for that particular basis input, but interference for a superposed input depends on complex sums across columns. Rounded display values should not be used as a substitute for full-precision verification. Accessibility and motion Use numerical readouts and tables when 3D motion makes comparison difficult. Focused and all-qubit modes should remain usable without depending on a subtle animated highlight. Respect reduced-motion preferences for decorative transitions where supported. The README offers static posters because a GIF itself does not inherit the browser's reduced-motion media query. Close Explorer or the assistant for more space when comparing a dense matrix or multiple spheres. The goal is a clear scientific reading, not maximum animation density. Report clipped labels with the viewport dimensions and view mode so the layout can be reproduced. Troubleshooting visual conclusions If a sphere appears centered, check purity and the known global state before assuming a rendering error. If a matrix is empty above four qubits, that is the display cap. If sampled and ideal views disagree, read noise settings and shot count. If an outcome label seems reversed, inspect classical measurement mapping. For exact comparisons, use the result data and the measurement(../quantum/measurement.md), Bloch(../quantum/bloch-spheres.md), and matrix(../quantum/unitary-matrices.md) lessons.

title: Studio: editing and workspace organization
text: Studio: editing and workspace organization Studio is the authoring surface for QORE. It combines Explorer, Monaco editing, file paths, execution actions, settings, and the lower command console. Its job is to keep the identity of the active source clear while letting you move into numerical inspection or compiler review without losing editing context. !Studio concept(../assets/animations/studio.gif) A deliberate starting point A new browser workspace opens with an empty Explorer. The welcome logo animates and the welcome closes automatically; no click-to-enter action is required. Get Started creates a single three-qubit learning circuit only when selected. Create blank file gives you an empty buffer. These are different choices, so onboarding never silently populates the workspace with unrelated demonstrations. Files created through Explorer remain editable browser-workspace records when saved. They are distinct from named backend projects and immutable Ledger experiments. A workspace file is editable working material; a Ledger snapshot records an experiment at a particular time. Treating the two as separate makes it possible to keep improving source without rewriting past results. Explorer and paths Explorer supports file and folder creation, selection, rename, deletion, and organization. Selecting a file opens its source in the editor. A file has a stable identifier even when its path changes. Folder renames update descendant paths atomically on the server, so a subtree is either moved consistently or left unchanged. Paths are relative to the account workspace. A path such as research/qaoa.qasm is a private database entry, not a route to an arbitrary server file. The visible path and console pwd action identify the active source. JSON and Markdown can be edited as workspace content, but quantum execution remains limited to supported circuit source. Before renaming a populated folder, finish pending saves. Another tab can change a descendant, which advances the folder's relevant version and may make the rename stale. Resolve a version conflict rather than assuming a partial local tree represents the server. Read workspace recovery(../guides/workspace-files.md) for the database semantics. Editing behavior Monaco supplies syntax-aware editing and a familiar code surface. The editor runtime loads when needed after a file is opened, reducing the initial workbench load. Supported settings adjust editing behavior; disabled settings explain that they are not wired rather than implying that every preference affects execution. The application uses one permanent graphite palette with consistent contrast, font weight, rounded glass surfaces, and focus treatment. This avoids different product views interpreting a theme setting differently. Use editor preferences for readability, and keep code legible when a laptop viewport reduces available width. Source edits invalidate attached live parse, simulation, and optimization context. This rule is essential: an old histogram must not appear to be output from newly typed code. Historical records remain in the Ledger. If you want to compare before and after, save distinct evidence and label it, rather than relying on whichever chart was last visible. Save confirmation and concurrent editing Browser storage is the authority for editable Explorer source in the account-free release. The server workspace API separately protects versioned records and evidence. Wait for visible saved state before closing a tab, and export important source before clearing site data or moving to another browser profile. Each stored entry has an integer version. A changed write to an existing entry must match the server version; otherwise it returns a conflict. An identical retry is idempotent, so a connection retry does not create a duplicate edit. A trashed identifier cannot be resurrected through an ordinary save; use restore within the recovery window. If a conflict occurs, preserve the current buffer, inspect the newer server text, and choose how to reconcile them. Do not clear browser storage as the first response, because the outbox may contain the only copy of unsynchronized changes. The current quota is 1,000 entries including Trash, 16 MiB aggregate source, and 32 KiB per file. Execution from the editor Run Kernel sends the active circuit and selected settings to the backend. Parsing and simulation happen in the bounded circuit runtime, not in Monaco or unrestricted browser Python. The backend returns structured results or a sanitized error with a useful location where possible. For a minimal compatible file: python from qiskit import QuantumCircuit qc = QuantumCircuit(1, 1) qc.h(0) qc.measure(0, 0) This predicts equal ideal probabilities. Choose shots and seed, run, then read the actual output in Lab. Adding an unsupported import does not install a capability; it should produce a clear source error. The language reference(../reference/circuit-python.md) lists supported construction patterns and operations. Panel layout and console Lab and Forge occupy the workspace beside Explorer. Closing Explorer expands the main view with a restrained transition. The assistant opens in a dedicated secondary bar, keeping explanations adjacent to the current task. The lower console has terminal, output, problems, and debug information drawn from current application evidence. At smaller widths, prioritize the panel relevant to the task. A dense matrix benefits from closing auxiliary bars. A long error needs its own scroll region rather than being clipped by the outer layout. Reduced-motion preferences should suppress decorative movement where supported; the scientific meaning does not depend on animation. Deletion and safety Delete moves an entry into Trash for 48 hours. Undo restores the last deleted file or folder batch, while Trash exposes other recoverable entries. Folder restore validates all destinations before changing any record. If a destination is occupied, nothing is partially restored. Active source has no automatic expiry. Deleted content becomes inaccessible at the exact 48-hour cutoff and is physically purged on the cleanup schedule. This is separate from provider backups. Export important work before major reorganizations, and sign out on shared devices so the next account does not inherit visible private state. Troubleshooting Studio If a selected file appears blank, verify the account, path, and save state before creating another file with the same name. If typing is slow, test a smaller source and close expensive visual views; a 32 KiB file bound does not mean every graphical rendering has equal cost. If results vanish after an edit, that is the intended stale-evidence protection. If a rename fails, inspect conflicts and synchronize outstanding writes before retrying.

title: Terminal, Output, Problems, and Debug
text: Terminal, Output, Problems, and Debug QORE's lower console provides typed commands for the active circuit and attached results. Its glass surface and command history resemble a development console, but the supported interface is deliberately bounded. Commands call QORE actions or display actual application data. They do not provide a general operating-system shell inside the server container. Understand the four surfaces Terminal accepts a command and records its response. Output summarizes attached simulation or optimization evidence as structured text. Problems lists backend errors and parser warnings with a file and source location where available. Debug exposes current nonsecret application context such as active path, health, limits, versions, source hash, and run identifiers. These views share a source context. If you edit a file, previous live results clear. A console command requesting counts before a run should explain that no result is attached, not print canned sample counts. A successful-looking prompt does not imply that arbitrary commands were executed. Run and compile commands | Command | Action | | --- | --- | | help | Show the current supported command help | | run, simulate, qiskit run | Simulate active source using workspace settings | | transpile, opt, optimize, qiskit transpile | Request a Forge candidate using selected settings | | qiskit --version | Show server-reported dependency versions | | qiskit backends | Show last backend and reported engine limits | Commands use the active source and settings; they do not accept an alternate script path or arbitrary simulator flags. Set shots, seed, noise, and optimization level through the supported workspace controls. Running again while an operation is busy should report that state instead of silently creating unrestricted parallel jobs. The qiskit prefix identifies QORE shortcuts. It does not launch an installed Qiskit command-line executable. The reported versions come from the server's health information, and the backend description comes from actual attached evidence. Inspect real circuit evidence | Command | Data shown | | --- | --- | | qiskit draw | Parsed circuit operations | | metrics, qiskit metrics | Current circuit metrics | | statevector, qiskit statevector | Available ideal complex amplitudes | | unitary, qiskit unitary | Available circuit operator | | probs | Sampled probabilities | | counts | Actual shot counts | | ast | Parsed QORE-IR, not a Python AST dump | | status | Current health and engine limits | Statevector and unitary output obey their display limits. A missing matrix above four qubits is expected. ast is retained as a familiar shortcut, but the displayed object is the circuit intermediate representation used by the application. Read QORE architecture(../reference/architecture.md) for that representation's role. Work with the active buffer ls and pwd identify the active file/path context. cat displays the active source; an optional argument must refer to that active buffer. The console is not an unrestricted directory browser and does not expose other container files. Use Explorer to select another workspace file before inspecting it here. date, echo, and clear are console utilities. Command history is bounded. Use the help output as the authority for accepted syntax. Extra arguments to actions that take none should produce a clear warning rather than being interpreted as shell flags. Commands such as package installation, file deletion through a host shell, remote SSH, hardware submission, or an unrelated cloud CLI are not executed. Unsupported commands should say so. This boundary protects both users and the shared service from a misleading terminal that pretends to have capabilities it lacks. Error locations and source truth The parser can report a line and column for supported syntax failures. Problems associates the report with the active file and lets the user navigate to the relevant source region. Some backend failures have no precise source location, in which case a default location is only a navigation aid, not a diagnosis of that exact character. Console output redacts common credential patterns and keeps bounded logs. Do not deliberately paste secrets into echo or source to test redaction: detection patterns cannot guarantee that every possible secret format is recognized. Use synthetic test values in isolated tests. Output distinguishes simulation metadata from optimization metadata. A failed run is an error, not a zero-probability distribution. A compiler warning does not prove the candidate wrong, and a successful compilation does not prove it equivalent. Read the status and structured evidence together. A practical debugging sequence Run status to inspect health and limits. Use pwd to confirm the active path and cat to verify the intended source. Parse or run the circuit. Read Problems for a structured failure, or metrics and counts for successful evidence. Inspect statevector and unitary only when the size and question make them relevant. When reporting a bug, include sanitized command, error code, package versions, and minimal nonprivate source. Avoid complete raw logs that may contain user code. A screenshot of a prompt is weaker evidence than the actual structured output and source identity. Use troubleshooting(../guides/troubleshooting.md) to distinguish a console misunderstanding from a runtime or persistence failure.

title: Account-free workspace and browser boundaries
text: Account-free workspace and browser boundaries QORE currently opens without registration, email confirmation, OAuth, or a password. This keeps first use immediate and makes local or controlled demonstrations straightforward. It also changes the security model: a browser profile, rather than a verified person, is the workspace boundary. What persists Explorer source is stored in the browser and survives ordinary refreshes. The active file, folders, settings, and recovery state are restored from the same site profile. Backend projects, runs, and Ledger records use SQLite. The server assigns a random opaque cookie and uses it to choose a database namespace without trusting an owner ID from request JSON. The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and Secure on production HTTPS. JavaScript cannot read it. It contains no email, name, API token, or database credential. It is nevertheless a capability: another person using the same unlocked browser profile can reach the same QORE records. Shared computers Use a separate operating-system account or browser profile on a shared machine. Export important source before clearing site data, using private browsing, or moving to another device. There is no password-based recovery, email restore, or account transfer in this release. Do not store passwords, API keys, patient data, regulated data, or confidential research in circuit comments. Browser storage is not an encrypted vault. QI questions and attached context can be sent to the configured external model provider when the assistant is used. Server persistence SQLite survives process restarts only when QORE_DB_PATH points to durable storage. A Render service without a mounted disk can lose projects, runs, and Ledger records during replacement or redeployment. Browser Explorer files remain on the device, but that does not restore missing backend evidence. Operators should back up the database, test restoration, monitor disk capacity, and retain the same public origin. Changing domains creates a new cookie and browser-storage origin, which appears as a different workspace. Isolation test Automated tests create two independent browser clients, save records in one, and verify that the other receives empty lists and 404 responses for guessed record IDs. This establishes browser-scope isolation for application routes. It is not equivalent to authentication because control of a browser profile is sufficient to use its cookie. When authentication returns A future identity layer should migrate anonymous records only after explicit user confirmation. It must not silently assign a shared-browser workspace to the next person who signs in. The identity design must keep provider tokens server-side, preserve source-hash checks, and retain owner scoping for projects, runs, experiments, files, Trash, and rate limits. See workspace files(workspace-files.md), production operations(../PRODUCTION.md), and security(../operations/security.md) for the complete operational boundary.

title: Your first three-qubit experiment
text: Your first three-qubit experiment This lesson prepares and measures a three-qubit GHZ state. A short circuit gives a clear ideal prediction, correlated outcomes, and a useful distinction between the complete quantum state and each reduced qubit. Enter the code yourself, or use the explicit Get Started action; the documentation does not preload account files. Create and predict Create ghz.py and enter: python from qiskit import QuantumCircuit qc = QuantumCircuit(3, 3) qc.h(0) qc.cx(0, 1) qc.cx(1, 2) qc.measure(0, 0) qc.measure(1, 1) qc.measure(2, 2) H prepares qubit zero in equal superposition. Controlled-X operations correlate the remaining qubits. The ideal premeasurement state is ( |000 + |111 ) / sqrt(2). Each terminal measurement writes to the matching classical index. Only 000 and 111 have nonzero ideal probability, each one half. At 1,024 shots, counts should be around 512 each, not necessarily exactly 512. The seed supports repeating a configuration under the same software but does not change the statistical meaning. Execute and read the result Choose 1,024 shots, seed 42, and ideal statevector simulation. Run the kernel. Verify the reported backend and total shot count. Compare the sampled histogram with the analytic reference rather than judging it by visual symmetry alone. TVD is one summary of the observed distribution difference. Inspect the nonzero ideal amplitudes. Each has magnitude about 0.7071, with squared magnitude one half. Display values are rounded; the internal comparison uses greater precision. Source and settings stay attached to this result, and a later source edit clears the live view. Interpret the spheres and matrix The complete register is pure, but tracing out two qubits leaves each individual qubit maximally mixed. Its local Bloch vector has radius zero and purity 0.5. A vector at the center is the expected result. One sphere cannot show all correlations of an entangled register. Because this circuit has three qubits, QORE can also display its eight-by-eight unitary matrix. That matrix describes the unitary prefix on every basis input. It does not include measurement and is not a table of sampled probabilities. The statevector is only the matrix's action on the initialized input, so it contains less information than the complete operator. Use Forge and preserve evidence Request a compiler candidate in Forge. This circuit is already small, so fewer gates are not guaranteed. Read the resource conventions, operator comparison, and exact measurement mapping. An unavailable result is not validated. If you apply the candidate, run the changed source again before comparing histograms. Save the editable file and wait for confirmation. Save a named experiment with the current run, then reopen it through the Ledger. That snapshot remains unchanged when you later edit the workspace file. A clone or an explicit edit starts a new variation. Extend one variable at a time Replace the first H with qc.ry(0.6, 0). Predict that the two allowed outcomes now have unequal probabilities determined by the rotation. Run with the same shots and seed. Next add a modest readout-error setting and explain why sampled outcomes can appear outside the two ideal strings while the ideal state remains unchanged. Record source, shots, seed, method, and noise for each variation. This habit makes the lesson a reproducible experiment instead of a collection of unrelated screenshots. Continue with measurement ordering(../quantum/measurement.md), entanglement(../quantum/entanglement.md), and QAOA(../quantum/qaoa.md).

title: Getting started with QORE
text: Getting started with QORE QORE gives a quantum experiment a clear path from source to evidence. Studio is where you write and organize code. Quantum Lab runs a supported circuit and exposes its sampled output and ideal state. Forge creates a compiler candidate for comparison. Research Ledger preserves the source and results as immutable evidence. The optional assistant sits beside these views in its own secondary sidebar. Begin with your own workspace On a first visit, the animated welcome closes automatically. The fixed graphite interface stays consistent across views. Explorer initially contains no example files or projects. Create a blank file to start from scratch, or select Get Started to create one editable three-qubit learning circuit. That is an explicit action and is never repeatedly inserted on refresh. No account or sign-in is required. Editable files persist in the browser profile, and the backend assigns an opaque HttpOnly workspace cookie for browser-scoped projects, runs, and Ledger records. The cookie is not a verified identity, so use a separate browser profile on a shared computer and export important source before clearing site data. Navigate the workbench Explorer holds editable files and folders. Select a supported circuit file to open Monaco with its source and visible path. Lab and Forge appear beside Explorer and expand when it closes. The assistant opens in a secondary bar beside the current view. The console below the workspace accepts supported commands; Problems presents reported errors and warnings. On a laptop, close Explorer or the assistant when inspecting a dense matrix. Results regions scroll within their panels. Source editing and result inspection are separate activities: changing the active code clears live results that belong to the previous source. It does not rewrite earlier runs stored in the Ledger. Run a circuit A shot-based simulation requires terminal measurements. Confirm that the source uses the supported language(../reference/circuit-python.md), choose shots and seed, then run the kernel. The API parses the circuit into QORE-IR, validates limits, and runs Qiskit Aer in a bounded worker. Unsupported imports are compatibility errors. Installing a package does not make arbitrary source executable through the editor. Read the backend label and execution metadata before interpreting the chart. Counts should sum to the requested shots. Sampled probabilities divide those counts by shots. The ideal reference is computed separately from the noiseless unitary prefix under the same classical mapping. A finite difference between those distributions is expected even in ideal mode. Open State World for a spatial interpretation, then inspect Bloch vectors and matrices when the circuit size permits. Matrix display ends above four qubits; ideal local-state and amplitude displays end above six. Those display bounds differ from the ten-qubit simulation limit. Keep source and evidence Saving a file preserves editable source in browser storage. Saving an experiment preserves a separate SQLite historical snapshot with its source and attached execution evidence. A later file edit cannot alter the old snapshot. Name experiments according to the question you tested, such as GHZ baseline, 1024 shots, rather than treating every execution as interchangeable. Forge adds a deliberate review step. Compare the original and candidate, resource metrics, validation status, and measurement mapping. Apply a candidate only after reviewing its scope, then run the changed source for fresh sampled evidence. The compiler may change the gate basis without reducing gate count. Finish the session Wait for saved status before closing a tab. Export important source before clearing browser storage. On a shared computer, use a separate operating-system or browser profile because QORE intentionally has no account boundary in this release. Use Undo immediately after an accidental deletion, or open Trash to restore another eligible entry within 48 hours. Folder restore checks occupied paths. Active files have no automatic expiry. The first experiment(first-experiment.md) gives a complete prediction-to-Ledger walkthrough; troubleshooting(troubleshooting.md) separates storage, execution, provider, and interpretation problems.

title: A learning path through quantum experiments
text: A learning path through quantum experiments Use QORE to test a prediction, inspect evidence, and preserve a record. Start with circuits whose expected behavior you can calculate. Complex visualizations become easier to read when you already know what a one-qubit amplitude, a classical measurement bit, and a mixed local state mean. One qubit and sampling Begin with one qubit, one classical bit, and a terminal measurement. The empty unitary prefix yields zero. X yields one. H yields equal ideal probabilities. Vary shots and observe that sampled frequencies approach the prediction without becoming a mathematical guarantee for every run. Two H gates return the initial state. This is a first example of interference: coherent amplitudes combine before measurement. Compare H; Z; H with X. Relative phase can change a later histogram even when it leaves an earlier basis probability unchanged. Rotations and visual state Try ry(theta, 0) for several angles. Compare the Bloch vector and ideal probabilities. Create superposition before applying rz, then add H to make the phase observable through a final basis measurement. Explain which view describes a state and which describes a transformation. Read Bloch spheres(../quantum/bloch-spheres.md) and unitary matrices(../quantum/unitary-matrices.md). Avoid inferring an unknown state from a single histogram. QORE's ideal state is calculated from known source, whereas experimentally reconstructing a physical state would require additional measurements. Two and three qubits Prepare a Bell state with H and CX, then follow the three-qubit GHZ lesson. Inspect local purity and explain why a zero local vector can coexist with a pure global state. Swap classical measurement destinations and predict the displayed bitstrings before running. Compare a correlated distribution with an entangled pure state that has the same computational-basis counts. Those counts alone do not distinguish every quantum property. This is an opportunity to practice making claims supported by the available evidence rather than the visual effect. Algorithms and objective functions Use Grover search(../quantum/grover.md) to identify the oracle and diffusion step. Calculate the target outcome first. Then study QAOA(../quantum/qaoa.md), where the result is an expected classical objective, not simply the most attractive bitstring. For a graph cut, calculate a cut score for sampled strings and compare against uniform sampling. Keep graph, angles, shots, seed, and source together. A small simulator exercise demonstrates an algorithm workflow; it does not establish a speedup over a classical solver. Verification and reproducibility Use Forge on a circuit containing deliberate redundant gates. Compare metrics under one convention and inspect the operator validation. Save the original and candidate as separate experiments. Increasing shots reduces sampling uncertainty but cannot fix the wrong measurement mapping, source version, or noise interpretation. Finish by reading runtime limits(../reference/limits.md), security(../operations/security.md), and reproducibility(../quantum/reproducibility.md). Knowing where the model stops is part of learning a quantum tool. When a program exceeds the supported runtime, simplify its circuit-building portion for QORE and keep broader classical workflows in an appropriately configured external development environment.

title: Local development
text: Local development Local development uses the same React workbench and FastAPI routes as the hosted product. The API can serve a built frontend from one origin, or Vite can provide hot reload while proxying /api to Python. SQLite stores backend records; browser storage retains editable Explorer source. Install and build Use Python 3.11–3.13 and a Node.js release compatible with the pinned pnpm version in frontend/package.json. The backend constrains Qiskit 2 and a compatible Aer version. Keep the committed frontend lockfile authoritative. powershell py -3.12 -m venv .venv & .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".test,docs" Set-Location frontend pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm build Set-Location .. & .\scripts\start.ps1 Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The startup script checks the environment and frontend build, sets a workspace temporary directory, and binds to loopback. Stop it with Ctrl+C. A missing build should be fixed by building, not by assuming that an unrelated preview server represents the current code. Hot reload Start scripts/start.ps1 -Dev in one terminal. Run pnpm dev inside frontend in another. Open Vite's reported local URL. The frontend continues to call relative API routes, and its development proxy sends them to the Python server. Hot reload does not rebuild the release bundle. Run pnpm build before checking the single-origin production behavior. If an older interface appears, verify the address and server process first. Do not delete browser site data or databases as a routine troubleshooting shortcut; they may contain user work. Configuration boundaries Keep configuration in the ignored server environment. Read configuration(../reference/configuration.md) for identity, storage, public origin, host validation, and optional AI variables. Never prefix a backend secret with VITE_; Vite embeds those values in public static files. The frontend does not need a service-role database key or model-provider credential. The account-free SQLite runtime is intended for local, personal, demonstration, or controlled-access use. A confidential public multi-user service requires a reviewed identity and authorization layer. Optional SDK extras support separate operator experiments; they do not expand the public source interpreter's allowlist. Module orientation main.py wires routes, anonymous browser workspaces, and orchestration. quantum.py implements source parsing, IR, simulation, metrics, and equivalence. runtime.py and worker.py bound execution. workspace.py and store.py handle entries, concurrency, evidence, and recovery. Feature components and application state live under frontend/src. Read the frontend agent guidelines before UI edits. Keep source hashes, live-result invalidation, immutable snapshots, and request types consistent. Renaming a path must preserve its stable record ID. A stale write must fail rather than silently overwrite newer server text. Use temporary browser contexts and databases when checking these behaviors. Verify and build documentation Run backend regression tests, production acceptance, security checking, and frontend auditing from the root. Run browser tests with pnpm test:ui inside frontend. Fresh reports matter: a stale passing artifact says nothing about the current change. The docs extra installs the Markdown renderer. scripts/build_docs.py turns the Markdown pages into a separate static documentation site with navigation, search, table of contents, and copied local images. Check its --help interface before invoking it for another destination. Edit Markdown sources rather than generated HTML that the next build will replace.

title: Troubleshooting QORE
text: Troubleshooting QORE Separate browser state, storage confirmation, source compatibility, worker execution, provider connectivity, and interpretation when diagnosing a problem. Preserve source before clearing site data. A failure at one boundary does not prove that every layer is broken. Browser workspace and obsolete account screens QORE currently has no account or email-confirmation flow. If an account dialog appears, the browser is serving an obsolete frontend bundle. Rebuild the frontend, restart the API process, and verify the content-hashed assets referenced by frontend/dist/index.html. Do not clear site data until important Explorer source is exported. If the workspace appears new, verify the exact origin and browser profile. Localhost, 127.0.0.1, a Render hostname, and a custom domain are separate storage origins. Never send cookies, environment values, or provider credentials in a support message. Saving and missing files Confirm that the same browser profile and origin are open. Pending or failed server-save status does not erase the browser draft. Another tab may have advanced a server entry version. Export current text before reconciling copies. Check Trash after a deletion. Restore is available for 48 hours and fails atomically if a path is occupied. Resolve that path conflict before retrying. Expired content cannot be recovered by replaying an old write. Active entries have no automatic expiry. Source rejection Read the structured error and source location. Unsupported imports or expressions indicate a program outside the circuit allowlist. Reduce it to one circuit, supported gates, finite numeric parameters, and terminal measurements. Arbitrary functions, filesystem access, remote provider clients, reset, and measurement-controlled execution are not supported. Check all limits, including the 500-operation total that counts measurements and barriers. Shot-based simulation needs at least one explicit terminal measurement. A stabilizer simulator can reject a non-Clifford circuit even when it parses; choose a compatible method. Busy jobs and timeouts Each API process permits two simultaneous quantum jobs, a bounded admission wait, and a 30-second worker timeout. Retry after a short delay for busy responses. Reduce circuit complexity when work exceeds its execution budget. Repeated duplicate submissions consume browser-workspace budgets and can make a temporary issue worse. Operators should compare memory and duration against the hosting limits. Process-local budgets do not coordinate multiple replicas. Scaling requires shared admission control and monitoring, not simply increasing every limit. Unexpected charts or spheres Read source hash and execution metadata. Edited source intentionally invalidates old live output. Ideal amplitudes and Bloch vectors describe the noiseless premeasurement prefix, while noisy counts describe a separately configured sampled model. A zero local Bloch radius in a GHZ state is correct. Matrix display is limited to four qubits, and local-state displays to six. For reversed labels, inspect the mapping: highest classical bit appears on the left; c0 is on the right. Unmeasured classical bits are zero. More shots cannot repair a wrong mapping interpretation. Useful reports Report the view, sanitized error code, approximate time, browser/viewport, server-reported package versions, and a minimal nonprivate circuit. State expected versus observed behavior and whether a new blank file reproduces it. Do not attach environment files, provider credentials, private source, or complete raw provider logs. The testing guide(../operations/testing.md) explains how to reproduce numerical issues against isolated data.

title: Files, folders, saving, and recovery
text: Files, folders, saving, and recovery Explorer contains editable files and folders. Browser storage preserves the visible workspace across refreshes. Server workspace records use a stable UUID, relative path, source kind, version, timestamps, and an opaque browser scope. A path rename changes the location without pretending that the file is a new record. !Persistent files and recovery(../assets/animations/workspace.gif) Create and edit Create a file or folder in Explorer. Select a file to open its source and visible path. Python and QASM circuit files can run through the supported quantum pipeline. JSON and Markdown are editable content, but they do not become quantum programs merely because they appear beside a circuit. Use meaningful relative paths such as research/ghz.py. Path validation prevents parent traversal and unsafe host-filesystem access. A workspace path names a QORE record; it does not grant access to arbitrary files on the server. The console refers to the active buffer and its path, not the container's general filesystem. Save status and interruption Wait for saved status before closing a tab. Browser storage retains the editor source immediately. Pending means a secondary server write has not completed; failed means that action needs attention. Neither message deletes the browser draft. On reconnection, version checks protect newer server content. If another tab modified the record, a stale update returns conflict. Preserve your current text, inspect the server state, and decide which version to keep. Repeatedly resending the old version is not conflict resolution. Rename a subtree Folder renames rewrite descendant paths atomically. The database validates every affected destination before applying the change. Descendant edits also advance relevant folder versions, preventing a stale folder action from ignoring concurrent work below it. Finish pending file writes before a large reorganization. Avoid simultaneous renames in multiple tabs. Stable IDs keep the active file linked to its record when a rename succeeds. If any destination conflicts, the subtree remains unchanged; the UI should display the failure rather than a partly renamed tree. Delete and recover A delete removes an entry from active Explorer and records a deletion timestamp. Deleting a folder creates one batch for its active subtree. Primary-bar Undo restores the last deleted batch. Trash lets you inspect and restore another eligible file or folder. Recovery lasts exactly 48 hours from deletion. At the cutoff, the API and database deny access and restoration. Scheduled cleanup removes expired source rows every five minutes, with additional request cleanup. Backups follow a separate operator retention policy, so this window is not a claim about erasing every backup copy. Restore checks every path before changing a batch. If another record occupies a destination, nothing is partially restored. Rename the occupying record, then retry. Expired content cannot be recovered by sending a stale cached PUT. Tombstones retain opaque identity only, preventing old clients from recreating deleted source without keeping its original path or contents.
